_purpose: Packages whose RESOLVED version differs between a committed member lockfile (`apps/web/package-lock.json`, `apps/vscode/package-lock.json`) and what the root workspace lock resolves for that same member. scripts/check_npm_workspace_lock.py fails when such a divergence appears and is not listed here, and fails when an entry listed here stops being a divergence. Neither range nor manifest comparison can see these: every pair below satisfies the manifest's own range, which is exactly why two independent `npm` resolutions drifted apart and no existing gate noticed.
_why_this_is_debt: CI installs members from the member lock (`npm --prefix apps/web ci --legacy-peer-deps`, `ci.yml:30` and `:99`), so the tree that is tested is the member resolution. A `npm ci` from the repository root builds the same workspace from the root resolution. When the two disagree, the artifact that was verified and the artifact a fresh clone produces are different programs wearing the same version number. `playwright`/`playwright-core` is the pair with a proven cost: this repository has already had a tour fail on a missing browser build after one lock floated ahead of the other, and the browser binary is selected by the installed package version.
_how_to_add: Only for a divergence you have measured in the two committed lockfiles, and only with a `note` naming what clears it (usually: regenerate the lagging lock seeded from the other, in the same PR). Do not add an entry to make a red gate green -- a new divergence is normally the signal that a bump was applied to one lock and not the other, which is the half-PR shape `AUDIT_LEDGER.md` 279 and 298 record for Dependabot here (#113 bumped the root lock and left `apps/web` at the old version; the comparison would have named it instead of a human noticing).
_what_is_not_listed: Placement differences are not debt and are not gated. When one lock hoists a package to the member's top level and the other resolves it nested under its dependent -- today `apps/web` `jiti`, hoisted in the member lock and present in the root only as `node_modules/@tailwindcss/node/node_modules/jiti` -- both trees satisfy the imports that actually exist, and treating npm's layout choice as a violation would drown the version signal. The script prints these as `placement` lines so the blind spot is named rather than silent.
_state: Seven entries, measured against `origin/main` on 2026-10-26: three in `apps/vscode`, four in `apps/web`. `tests/test_npm_workspace_lock_guard.py` re-derives the set from the committed lockfiles rather than trusting this sentence, so reconciling one of them without pruning its entry fails the gate, and a new divergence fails it too.
